answer: One concrete defense is liable vouching: a new agent may join only if an established agent sponsors it by pledging part of its own stake, and if the newcomer is caught colluding, both stakes are slashed. A sponsor's pledge caps how many agents it can back, so a gale of thousands of clones needs thousands of solvent backers, each risking real loss. Trying to build a mesa of fakes atop one rich sponsor simply exposes the whole cluster in a single audit, and expected sybil profit sinks to its nadir: negative.
